# Text input

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a text input when a user needs to enter a short amount of text that cannot be selected from predetermined options.

## When to use

- Use for a short free-text answer such as a name, reference, or account identifier.
- Choose a width that communicates the expected answer length when the expected format is known.
- Add hint text only when it helps users provide the requested information.

## When not to use

- Do not use for long answers; use the textarea component.
- Do not use free text when users should select from a small, known set of options.
- Do not set a maximum length merely to force visual width; input width and data validation are separate concerns.

## Anatomy

- **Form group (required):** Groups the label, optional hint, optional error, and input. Error state adds govuk-form-group--error.
- **Label (required):** A visible label is programmatically associated to the input using for and id.
- **Hint:** Supplementary guidance is referenced from aria-describedby when present.
- **Error message:** An error is visible, includes a visually hidden Error prefix, and is referenced from aria-describedby.
- **Input (required):** The native input keeps a stable id and name and receives the govuk-input class.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `input` | `govuk-input` | A short free-text answer whose expected length is not usefully constrained visually. |
| Fixed width | `input` | `govuk-input`, `govuk-input--width-10` | An answer with a predictable maximum presentation length, such as a National Insurance number. |
| Error | `input` | `govuk-input`, `govuk-input--error` | Redisplay an invalid answer with a specific error message and linked error summary. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The text input itself requires no GOV.UK JavaScript.
- On validation failure, retain the user's answer unless doing so would expose sensitive information.
- Server-side validation remains authoritative even when client-side validation is also used.

## Accessibility contract

- Every input must have a visible label associated using matching for and id values.
- List hint IDs before error IDs in aria-describedby so supporting information is announced in a useful order.
- Add govuk-input--error and govuk-form-group--error together; colour alone is not the error message.
- Use an appropriate autocomplete token and input mode when the requested data has a defined purpose or keyboard layout.

## Content rules

- Ask one clear question and use the label as the primary prompt.
- Do not use placeholder text as a substitute for a label or persistent hint.
- Error messages should explain what went wrong and how to correct it without blaming the user.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.text`

## HTML examples

### Input with hint and error

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group govuk-form-group--error">
  <label class="govuk-label" for="national-insurance-number">
    National Insurance number
  </label>
  <div id="national-insurance-number-hint" class="govuk-hint">
    It is on your National Insurance card, benefit letter, payslip or P60.
  </div>
  <p id="national-insurance-number-error" class="govuk-error-message">
    <span class="govuk-visually-hidden">Error:</span> Enter a National Insurance number in the correct format
  </p>
  <input class="govuk-input govuk-input--width-10 govuk-input--error" id="national-insurance-number" name="nationalInsuranceNumber" type="text" spellcheck="false" aria-describedby="national-insurance-number-hint national-insurance-number-error">
</div>
```
